Experience 1–4 Years of Experience)

About the Role 

We are looking for a highly proactive, self-motivated, and solution-oriented AI Workflow Engineer to join our team. This isn’t a passive execution role—we need a builder who requires minimal oversight, thinks critically about our current operational roadblocks, and can actively lead the charge in transforming our workflows, processes, and systems into an AI-first, agentic paradigm. 

Because our core operations and primary client environment are deeply integrated with a major global search giant's ecosystem, you will be building solutions that interface smoothly with enterprise-grade cloud, data, and developer tooling. You will bring fresh perspectives, industry-proven patterns, and hands-on experience in modern AI tooling to help us level up our projects and reinvent how work gets done. If you love jumping into complex systems, identifying bottlenecks, and architecting autonomous or semi-autonomous multi-agent workflows, this role is for you. 

Key Responsibilities 

Process Audit & Transformation: Analyze existing manual and semi-automated workflows to identify high-impact areas ripe for AI-driven transformation. 
Agentic Architecture Design: Design, build, and deploy multi-agent systems and pipelines using modern orchestration frameworks (e.g., LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, or custom agent loops) that can execute multi-step tasks autonomously. 
Ecosystem-Aligned Integration: Build workflows and leverage APIs that integrate cleanly within enterprise environments, utilizing cloud storage, serverless pipelines, and modern developer tooling. 
Proactive Innovation & Ideation: Bring ideas, architectural suggestions, and process improvements to the table to level up our engineering projects and internal operations. 
Continuous Optimization: Monitor agent performance, refine prompts, manage token usage/costs, evaluate guardrails, and optimize execution speed and accuracy across agentic loops. 

Candidate Requirements 

1. Experience & Background 

Technical Experience: 1 to 4 years of hands-on technical experience in software engineering, AI/ML engineering, or workflow automation. 
LLM Deployment: Demonstrated track record of building and deploying functional applications or automation pipelines leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs) (e.g., Gemini / Google Cloud AI APIs, OpenAI, Anthropic, or open-source models). 
Agentic Frameworks: Hands-on project experience with agentic frameworks or orchestration tools (e.g., LangChain, LangGraph, CrewAI, LlamaIndex, or AutoGen). 

2. Mindset & Behavioral Traits (Non-Negotiable) 

Proactive Self-Starter: Highly motivated and autonomous; you thrive when given high-level objectives and take full ownership of figuring out the "how." 
Solution-Oriented: You view roadblocks as engineering puzzles and instinctively design smarter, automated alternatives. 
Idea Generator: You actively bring insights, suggest industry best practices, and challenge the status quo to elevate our team's capabilities. 

3. Technical Stack & Skills 

Programming: Proficient in Python and familiarity with JavaScript/TypeScript/Rust where helpful. 
AI/ML & Cloud Tooling: Hands-on experience with prompt engineering, function calling / tool use, RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation), vector databases, and enterprise cloud ecosystems (Google Cloud / AWS / Azure). 
APIs & Integration: Experience building and consuming RESTful APIs, webhooks, and integrating third-party productivity tools (Slack, GitHub, Notion, databases, etc.) into agent ecosystems. 
Workflow Logic: Strong understanding of state management, error handling, and asynchronous programming required for reliable multi-agent loops. 

What We Offer 

High Autonomy: Direct ownership over defining and shaping our agentic workflows with minimal bureaucracy. 
Frontier Tech: Opportunity to work directly at the frontier of AI agent orchestration within a top-tier enterprise ecosystem. 
Fast-Paced Growth: A culture that rewards proactive problem-solvers and fast execution.

Our mission is to radically transform healthcare delivery by harnessing the power of artificial intelligence and clinical expertise to make care more affordable, accessible, and effective for everyone. Patients interact with advanced AI systems at every step of their care and follow-up. Licensed physicians review each case with the patient for the clinical decision in our integrated virtual clinic.

As a member of the technical staff on the artificial intelligence engineering team, you will design, build, and ship ML and LLM systems (agentic AI workflows) that directly shape how clinicians and patients interact with our platform. Sister Concern of AC Infotech INC (USA) (www.acinfotech.com)
Job Title: Gen AI Engineer
Position: Full Time / Permanent
Mode: Remote
Location: Karur / Dharwad


Job Description:
Experience Required: 5 - 15 Years


Responsibilities:
Core AI engineering (must-have)
LLM application design. Prompt engineering, tool/function calling, structured output, and agent patterns, plus judgment about when an LLM is the wrong tool.
Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). Chunking strategies, embeddings, vector stores, retrieval tuning, and grounding answers with citations.
Evaluation. Building test sets and LLM-as-judge or golden-answer evals, and measuring hallucination, accuracy and latency. This is the biggest gap between people who've done demos and people who've shipped.
Responsible AI and guardrails. PII and PHI handling, which matters a lot in insurance and disability claims. Also prompt-injection defense, content filtering and audit logging.
Languages. Strong Python, plus either TypeScript/Node or Java. Java helps here because of the Spring Boot / JBoss estate.
CI/CD for AI assets. Versioning prompts, bot definitions, contact flows and knowledge base content the same way as code. Promoting Lex bots and Connect flows Dev QA UAT Prod through pipelines. Running evals as a pipeline quality gate.


AWS: contact center and AI services
Amazon Connect. Contact flows, routing profiles and queues, Lambda integrations, Contact Lens (transcripts and sentiment), Amazon Q in Connect (agent assist), CTR/contact data streaming.
Amazon Kinesis. Familiar with streaming concepts and use in conversational AI applications.
Amazon Lex V2. Intents, slots, utterance design, confidence thresholds, fallback handling, versions and aliases, and multi-language bots. Bonus if they've used generative features like assisted slot resolution or QnAIntent.
Amazon Bedrock. Model selection, Knowledge Bases (data sources, sync, chunking config, OpenSearch Serverless or Aurora pgvector), Agents, Guardrails, and Flows.
Workflow orchestration. Step Functions, EventBridge, Lambda, SQS/SNS, and knowing when to use Bedrock Flows or Agents versus plain Step Functions.
Platform fundamentals. IAM (least privilege, cross-account roles; Lex and Connect access is tightly controlled here), VPC basics, CloudWatch and X-Ray, S3, DynamoDB, KMS, and cost awareness for token and Connect usage.
Infrastructure as code. Terraform preferred (or CDK/CloudFormation). Connect and Lex are notoriously hard to manage as code, so ask how they handled promoting contact flows and bots between environments.
ElevenLabs. Experience working with ElevenLabs API for agentic voice models, workflows, configuration, testing, and more.
Deepgram. Familiarity with Deepgram and/or similar STT services and implementation.


Azure DevOps and software engineering
Azure Repos. Git branching strategies (feature/release/hotfix), PR workflow, branch policies, code review discipline.
Azure Pipelines. YAML multi-stage pipelines, templates, variable groups, service connections to AWS (OIDC or role assumption), environments with approvals and gates, and artifact feeds.
Engineering practices. Unit and integration testing, mocking LLM calls, SonarCloud/static analysis, secrets management, and working in ADO Boards (stories, acceptance criteria).
Controlled-change mindset. Experience in a regulated environment: change records, audit trails, separation of duties.
Application Health Monitoring. Use of Data Dog and or CloudWatch to monitor an application’s health, provide warning and alert messages for proactive management. Manage incidents include defining incident playbooks.







Thanks & Regards

Yazhini Subramanian
Recruitement Team

Mindpro Technologies Pvt Ltd (www.mindprotech.com)
Tel no: 8220917422

Job Summary

You will build the AI features that make those products work and you will build them for production, not for a demo.

That means retrieval systems over large document corpora that arrive as inconsistent PDFs, scans and HTML. Extraction pipelines that pull structured fields out of documents that were never designed to be parsed. Classification against real-world taxonomies. Agentic workflows where they genuinely beat a deterministic pipeline. And, underneath all of it, the evaluation harnesses that tell you whether any of it actually works.

Because you will work across several ventures rather than one, you will also be one of the people deciding what gets built once and reused everywhere. That leverage is the most interesting part of the job.

This is an engineering role. Most of your time goes into services, pipelines, data plumbing, tests and evals. The model is a component, not the job.

Responsibilities
Take AI features from vague problem statement through to specified, built, evaluated and deployed.
Build RAG systems end to end ingestion, parsing, chunking, embedding, retrieval, reranking, grounding and citation over messy documents at scale.
Build extraction and classification pipelines that map unstructured documents onto structured taxonomies, and handle the long tail where documents dont cooperate.
Build evaluation harnesses, golden datasets and regression suites, and feed real production failures back into them.
Own cost and latency as first-class constraints: model routing, caching, batching, context economy, fallbacks when a provider degrades.
Ship with real observability tracing, quality dashboards, spend tracking.
Identify whats common across ventures and build it once, properly, with documentation.
What we're looking for
2-4 years of professional software engineering, including at least a year building with language models. Strong engineering fundamentals matter more here than exotic ML knowledge.
Youve shipped an LLM-powered feature to real users in production and can describe it end to end-the data flow, the failure handling, what it cost, what broke after launch, and what you changed. Notebooks, demos and course projects dont count for this one.
Evaluation discipline: you can explain how you knew a system was good enough to ship, and how you measured whether changes made it better. The dataset, the metric, the baseline.
Strong Python, plus real production practice: version control, testing, CI, containers, and operating a service you wrote. Comfort with SQL and a cloud platform.
